subject: FinOpsCo: pricing & batching sprint — token volumes + next steps
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Liu <hannah@finopsco.com>
Cc: Eli Turner <eli.turner@finopsco.com>; aditya_rao@redwood.com; monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 20 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: FinOpsCo: pricing & batching sprint — token volumes + next steps

Hi Hannah / Eli,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the clear signal on cost sensitivity and the mixed workload shape you described. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can align the POC sprint: 

Key notes from the call:
- Workload mix: ~70% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 25% mid-length (65–512 tokens), 5% long-form generation (512–8k tokens).
- Expected steady state: ~8–12M tokens/day in month 1, with burst windows up to 250 concurrent requests in 10–15m spikes.
- Primary goals: validate sustained $/1M token near your target, and confirm 95th percentile latency <300ms for short prompts under expected concurrency.

Commercial guardrails you mentioned:
- Target unit-econ: $75–$95 per 1M tokens (inclusive of streaming/response tokens) for the steady baseline.
- Procurement threshold: need an initial committed monthly budget band (you suggested $20k–$40k/mo) to trigger reserved capacity discussion.

Technical considerations we propose validating in the sprint:
1) Continuous batching behavior with mixed short/long distribution — ensure short prompts aren’t held beyond 10ms median queueing.
2) Concurrency shaping — route short prompt traffic to low-latency pool while allowing long-form to drain on background nodes.
3) KV/prefix caching for repeat-context patterns to reduce token generation on assistant-style prompts.
4) Quantization profile benchmark (FP16 vs int8-like path) to measure cost delta and any quality regressions on your evaluation set.

Proposed POC plan (2-week sprint):
- Week 0 (this week): share volume breakdown (attached) and confirm sample prompt sets + 24h peak logs export.
- Week 1: Redwood runs baseline throughput tests with your sample mix on hosted dedicated pool; capture token-cost curves at 1M, 5M, 10M daily volumes and measure latency percentiles.
- Week 2: Tune batching window and concurrency rules; run a 48h soak during a simulated spike; deliver results + recommended pricing bands and an ops playbook for continuous batching.

Action items for FinOpsCo:
- Send the 7-day sample traffic CSV and a short list (10–20) of representative prompts for each bucket. (Attachment: finops_volume_breakdown.xlsx — placeholder).
- Confirm whether Procurement needs an MSA/PDF before POC starts.

Internal note: Aditya / Monica — can you validate that our low-latency pool will honor <15ms batching waits for short ops and that we can expose a traffic-splitting policy for short vs long? If not, list limitations before Monday.

Hannah — if that plan looks good I’ll schedule the kickoff for Monday 2/22 and share the redwood_poc_instructions.pdf.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
T: +1 415-555-0198

Attachments: finops_volume_breakdown.xlsx (spreadsheet — volume buckets), redwood_poc_instructions.pdf (POC runbook)

Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinOpsCo: pricing & batching sprint — token volumes + next steps

Thanks Tessa — this looks great and aligned with internal expectations. Quick clarifications:

1) Volume confirmation: attached is our 7-day sample export (separate secure upload), aggregated to the same buckets you used. The projected steady state for month 1 is 10M tokens/day; we see daily variability +/- 20%.
2) Budget: procurement is comfortable committing to a $25k–$35k/month band for the initial quarter if we can show near the $80/1M tokens profile.
3) Latency: 95th < 300ms for short prompts is a hard requirement for product adoption.

Procurement note (Procurement): please confirm if an NDA/MSA is required before the technical POC. We prefer to avoid heavy redlines for a proof-of-technical-fit.

We approve the kickoff on Monday 2/22 — please send calendar invite + runbook.

—Hannah
Hannah Liu
Director, Product Operations | FinOpsCo
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 22 Feb 2027 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: FinOpsCo: pricing & batching sprint — internal check on batching windows

Tessa / Monica — quick feasibility notes after looking at the provided buckets and expected spike shape: 

- Short prompt bucket (70%) — we can keep batching wait <=12ms median by assigning a dedicated micro-pool (n1-small-latency) and setting continuous batching window to 8–12ms. That meets the 95th <300ms target as long as the concurrency is split appropriately.
- Spike handling — for 250 concurrent bursts we recommend a short-pool autoscale headroom to 4x baseline; otherwise we’ll see queue growth that impacts tail latency.
- Long-form throughput — route to compute-dense nodes with a 30–50ms batching window to maximize token efficiency; this will push cost down for long tokens at the expense of some latency (acceptable for long runs).

Caveats:
- If FinOpsCo requires strict single-tenant isolation on long-form nodes (for billing/segmentation), we’ll need an extra reserved slab which shifts economics slightly.
- Quantization to int8-like path yields ~18–24% cost reduction on generator tokens; we should run quality regression on their eval set before committing pricing.

I’ll prep an ops config diff and a short test plan (throughput targets + latency checkpoints) to attach to the kickoff invite.

-Aditya
Principal Systems PM | Redwood Inference

Hannah / Eli / Procurement team,

Thanks — appreciate the swift turnaround. We’ll proceed with Monday kickoff: 2027-02-22 10:00 PT (calendar invite sent). What we’ll deliver in the initial POC run:

Deliverables:
- A 48–72 hour throughput report covering: token consumption at 1M/5M/10M/day curves, per-token unit cost estimates, and latency percentiles per bucket.
- Recommended runtime config for continuous batching + concurrency routing (including autoscale headroom numbers).
- A short regression report on quality for int8-like quantization on the sample eval set.
- Ops playbook with escalation flow and rollback thresholds.

Next steps for Procurement: if you can confirm NDA/MSA status by EOD Wednesday we’ll share a lightweight POC addendum (DocuSign link in the invite) that covers limited-term commit and billing mechanics for the reserved headroom used during the POC. If Procurement prefers no contract, we can run a purely technical POC on hosted credits with throttled capacity — tradeoffs documented in the runbook.

I’ve attached a POC results CSV template (poc_results_template.csv) to help standardize outputs — you can drop it into the shared drive folder.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,

Tessa Morgan
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
